question:
A particle moves through the first quadrant as follows. During the first minute it moves from the origin to \((1,0).\) Thereafter, it continues to follow the directions indicated in the figure, going back and forth between the positive \(x\) and \(y\) axes, moving one unit of distance parallel to an axis in each minute. At which point will the particle be after exactly \(1989\) minutes?

[Figure 1](figures/1989_AMC_12_Q23_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The points \((n,n)\) are useful checkpoints because the particle turns there. From the arrows, it reaches \((1,1)\) after \(2\) minutes, then \((2,2)\) after \(6\) minutes, then \((3,3)\) after \(12\) minutes. We can justify the pattern by tracking the journey between consecutive checkpoints.

For an odd positive integer \(n\), the route from \((n,n)\) goes left \(n\) units, up \(1\), and right \(n+1\), reaching \((n+1,n+1)\). For even \(n\), it goes down \(n\), right \(1\), and up \(n+1\). Either journey takes
\[
n+1+(n+1)=2(n+1)
\]
minutes, since each unit takes one minute. Including the first \(2\) minutes, the time of arrival at \((n,n)\) is therefore
\[
T_n=2+4+\cdots+2n=n(n+1).
\]
Here \(1+2+\cdots+n=n(n+1)/2\), obtained by pairing the sum with its reverse.

Now
\[
T_{44}=44\cdot45=1980,
\qquad T_{45}=45\cdot46=2070.
\]
Thus minute \(1989\) comes \(9\) minutes after the visit to \((44,44)\). Because \(44\) is even, the next segment goes downward for \(44\) minutes. Since \(9<44\), the particle is still on that segment, at
\[
(44,44-9)=\boxed{(44,35)},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
